To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the expression of a number of proteins involved in the regulation of neurotransmission, synaptic plasticity and actin dynamics is regulated in a strain‐specific manner, and 2) the protein expression pattern can be used to classify different mouse strains.

(1) the expression of proteins involved with neurotransmission and actomyosin activity‐dependent remodelling is strain‐dependent in mouse hippocampal tissue and (2) the expression of some of these proteins is correlated with the level of hippocampal long‐term potentiaion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of strain‐dependent regulation of protein expression involved in neurotransmission as well as in activity‐induced cytoskeletal changes in mouse brain.
the identification of strain‐dependent protein expression patterns in the hippocampus of five inbred strains of the mouse.
the analysis of the molecular mechanisms of the brain function and its genetic regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proteomic approach used herein has the potential to be a useful tool to investigate strain‐dependent regulation of proteins involved in neuronal information processing.
the strain‐dependent expression pattern of the analysed proteins is a reflection of strain differences in the hippocampal proteome.
strain‐dependent regulation of the proteins analysed in this study may contribute to the observed differences in behaviour, cognition and long‐term memory between the mouse strains investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strain‐dependent regulation of proteins related to neurotransmission and actomyosin‐mediated cytoskeleton remodelling is a common phenomenon in mouse brain.
the proteome is a promising source of information for the understanding of the molecular mechanisms of brain function and dysfunction.
the proteome of the brain can be used as an indicator of the genetic elements responsible for the phenotypic difference between mouse strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of proteins related to neuronal information handling in the brain is not uniform across different inbred mouse strains.
proteomics could serve as a powerful tool for the identification of genetic and physiological factors that contribute to phenotypic differences in brain function between different strains of mice.
proteomics is an excellent tool to study the molecular mechanisms underlying the genetic basis of behaviour and cognition.
